articles.title: A working-class Alaskan Native takes on a ‘multimillionaire’ Republican for seat in Congress
articles.summary:
Independent candidate Bill Hill is threatening to unseat Trump ally Nick Begich with a message of affordability

As Republicans…

blocks.text: As Republicans fight to maintain their narrow majority in Congress, they face a unique challenge in Alaska – not from a Democrat, but from an independent commercial fisher and first-time candidate running to flip the state’s lone House seat.

Bill Hill, who is an Alaska Native and has worked in education and construction, has positioned himself as a working-class candidate who will fight to make life more affordable for people like himself and his family.

Like voters across the country, Alaskans are deeply worried about affordability and rising cost of basic necessities. Hill counts himself among the voters who have felt squeezed by high fuel prices driven up by Donald Trump’s war on Iran.

“When the spring fuel barge showed up in my home town of Naknek this spring, I went from paying $118 to fill my truck up to over $200,” Hill said. “Our gas went from $6.70 a gallon to almost $9 a gallon.”

Hill’s campaign to unseat the Republican congressman Nick Begich has gained momentum in the final weeks before the 3 November election, as national Democrats line up behind him and ad spending ramps up. The nonpartisan Cook Political Report recently shifted the race from “likely Republican” to “leans Republican”, with the district favoring Republicans by 6%.

Recent polls showed Hill trailing Begich by single digits, but Hill’s support grows when voters learn more about his background, as he works to boost his name recognition. The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee added the race to its coveted “red to blue” program in September.

Hill has not specified whether he would caucus with Democrats if elected. This cycle, he is among several independents challenging Republicans in red states, including Senate candidates Dan Osborn in Nebraska and Todd Achilles in Idaho.

In Alaska, Begich may benefit from being the only Republican in the four-way general election contest run under the state’s ranked-choice system. Polls suggest support for Democrat Eric Hafner, who is serving time in a federal prison in New York and has no apparent links to the state, could complicate Hill’s path.
Hill has staked his campaign on his ability to personally relate to the economic pain and frustrations of his fellow Alaskans.

“I have spent a life being in the ditches, in the school hallways, on the back decks of fishing boats with hard-working people, running a small business like so many Alaskans do, and I know what the struggles and challenges that we face are,” Hill said. “I also know what our hopes and dreams are.”

He noted the cost of heating fuel nearly doubled, from $4.50 a gallon to $8.30, while price increases in some of Alaska’s more remote villages have soared even higher. In places such as Ambler and Shungnak, Indigenous villages that sit along the Kobuk River near the Arctic circle, the price of a gallon of gas has surpassed $25.
“This is crushing Alaskans,” Hill said. “We are feeling the crunch every single day.”

More than one in three Alaskan households aren’t earning enough income to cover housing, food, childcare and other essential expenses, according to a report by the United Way of Anchorage and Alaska 211 published earlier this month.

In 2024, Begich, the conservative son of a prominent Democratic family in Alaska, narrowly ousted the incumbent Democrat, Mary Peltola, who is currently running for US Senate. Though Trump won the state by a resounding 13%, Begich prevailed by just 2.4%.
Like Peltola, Hill is a supporter of gun rights, in line with Alaska’s strong hunting tradition, and is a supporter of both the oil industry and the renewable energy industry.

Hill cited the impacts on Alaskans of cuts to the Snap nutrition-assistance program and Medicaid, the expiration of Affordable Care Act tax credits, Trump’s tariffs, federal job losses in Alaska, and the cancellation of several Alaskan renewable energy projects by the Trump administration as contributing factors to added costs facing Alaskans, with many of the cuts enacted by the president’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act set to go into effect in 2027.
after newsletter promotion
“It is getting very, very difficult for working people in Alaska to get by,” Hill said, charging that his opponent was a “multimillionaire working for billionaires”.

With his reported assets valued at $119,000, Hill has sought to highlight the vast wealth gap between himself and his opponent, who’s worth at least $7.4m. “He’s somebody who doesn’t represent the everyday Alaskan in his work,” Hill added.
Begich’s office did not respond to multiple requests for comment, but previously denied his wealth affects his voting record.

“Congressman Begich’s personal finances have no impact on his legislative decisionmaking process,” Silver Prout, a spokesperson for Begich’s congressional office, told the Anchorage Press in an email.
Begich praised the passage of Trump’s One Big beautiful Bill Act, calling it a “transformative victory”, and has continued supporting Trump’s war in Iran.

Hill, a Dena’ina Athabascan Native Alaskan, has worked as a commercial fisherman since he was eight years old and continues to do so. He has also worked union construction jobs with Laborers’ Local 341, and worked for 25 years in education as a union member teacher, principal and school district superintendent.
Alaska has one of the highest union density rates in the US. As of 2025, 18.1% of all workers in the state were union members, the third highest rate in the US, behind Hawaii and New York.

More than 20 labor organizations, including the Alaska AFL-CIO, have endorsed Hill’s campaign. Begich, meanwhile, has signed on to the National Right to Work Act and has a 0% lifetime voting score by the AFL-CIO, the largest federation of labor unions in the US.

“Unions need more support in Congress, and we see attacks on trying to tear down their power in this nation,” Hill said. “At the end of the day, unions built the middle class of this country, and they’re the ones who can do it again.”

articles.title: 19 more Philippine restos get Michelin Guide recognition
articles.summary: On its second edition in the Philippines, the Michelin Guide recognized 19 new food establishments across Manila, Cebu, Pampanga and Cavite, bringing the number of honorees this year to 127.

blocks.text: October 31, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — On its second edition in the Philippines, the Michelin Guide recognized 19 new food establishments across Manila, Cebu, Pampanga and Cavite, bringing the number of honorees this year to 127.
The new additions across Manila, Cebu, Pampanga and Cavite were cited by the gastronomy recognition body for their world-class culinary identity.

“Manila continues to lead with chef-driven restaurants, tasting menus, and ambitious contemporary concepts, while Cebu draws strength from its lechon, seafood, charcoal-grilled dishes, and convivial home cooking,” the Michelin Guide said.

Makati-based restaurant Helm retained its two-Michelin stars, while Asador Alfonso, Celera, Gallery by Chele, Hapag, Inatô, Kása Palma, Linamnam and Toyo Eatery maintained its one-Michelin star distinction.

Flow in Makati joined the guide with a one-star distinction for the extensive use of local ingredients that create “varied textures and layered sauces to craft flavors that are innovative and harmonious.”
Meanwhile, Michelin recognized 31 establishments as Bib Gourmand up from its 25 awardees last year.

Among the new Bib Gourmand food places are Apag Marangle and Tito Boy in Pampanga, Balay Dako and Bawai’s Vietnamese Kitchen in Cavite, Azela in Manila, Tatang’s Lechon and Kalipay in Cebu and C.H.E Bacolod Chicken House Express in Makati.
Ato-ah in Cebu and Butcher Boy in Las Piñas were promoted to Bib Gourmand from the Selected list last year.
Under the Michelin Selected, 86 establishments were named this year, up from 74 in the inaugural edition.

The 18 newly recognized were Abé (Taguig), Bombvinos Bodega, Cyria’s Kandingan, Digámo, Elaia by Cyma, Haliya, Idalia, Kokeek’s Manokan, Kong, Kumedor, Liyab, Makanai, Marjo’s Pochero, Mila’s Tokwa’t Baboy (San Andres), Oyster Bay, Playa, Souq and Tadhanà.

Michelin also awarded former overseas Filipino worker Chef Frances Tariga of Tadhanà with the Opening of the Year recognition and former seafarer Chef Francis Lacson of Digámo with the Young Chef award.
Chef Clyde Joshua Zafra of Tito Boy received the service award while bar beverage manager Ron Job Sanchez of Automat was given the Exceptional Cocktails Award.
In a speech, President Marcos said the government will support culinary education for aspiring chefs and hospitality professionals to strengthen the industry.

articles.title: P30 million cloud-seeding brings hope to Visayas sugar farms
articles.summary: As the Visayas sugar industry braces for the looming threat of a projected super El Niño, a much-needed dose of hope may soon come from the skies.

blocks.text: October 31, 2026 | 12:00am

The Sugar Regulatory Administration (SRA) is setting aside P30 million for cloud-seeding operations in the Visayas, particularly in Negros Island and Panay, to help ease the impact of prolonged dry conditions on sugarcane farms.
STAR / File
BACOLOD CITY, Philippines — As the Visayas sugar industry braces for the looming threat of a projected super El Niño, a much-needed dose of hope may soon come from the skies.
United Sugar Producers Federation (UNIFED) president Manuel Lamata said he received a letter from SRA administrator Pablo Luis Azcona, dated Oct. 26, confirming the funds have been allocated.
The cloud-seeding operations are expected to begin this November.
Lamata expressed gratitude to Azcona for taking early action, saying the industry hopes the funding will be enough to help sugar farmers weather the difficult months ahead.

Lamata thanked Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel for funding cloud-seeding operations last month and for announcing the Department of Agriculture will provide additional funding for similar efforts next year.
For sugarcane farmers already facing drought, pest infestation and rising fuel and farm-input costs, every drop of rain could make a difference.
Lamata said the actions of Azcona and Laurel demonstrate their concern for the sugar industry, particularly during a challenging period for farmers and workers.

articles.title: VP camp calls out new ‘tanim witness’
articles.summary: The camp of Vice President Sara Duterte yesterday dismissed the claim of an alleged former driver of former House speaker Lord Allan Velasco, that he delivered suitcases of cash to her.

blocks.text: October 31, 2026 | 12:00am
Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte arrives before the start of the impeachment trial at the Senate of the Philippines in Pasay, Metro Manila on July 7, 2026.
AFP / Noel Celis

MANILA, Philippines — The camp of Vice President Sara Duterte yesterday dismissed the claim of an alleged former driver of former House speaker Lord Allan Velasco, that he delivered suitcases of cash to her.

Duterte’s spokesperson Paolo Panelo reacted after the former driver of Velasco, identified with the alias “Chris,” arrived at the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) on Thursday to submit his affidavit against Duterte.

“Another day, another tanim (planted) witness. They can keep manufacturing allegations, but they cannot fabricate the truth,” Panelo said in a statement. “As before, VP Sara will happily dismantle each allegation with evidence at the proper time.”
The spokesperson also asked the media not merely to report, but to independently test and verify these claims.
“That way, they can see for themselves how the Fourth Estate is being weaponized for the relentless, but ultimately ineffective, black propaganda against the Vice President,” Panelo added.
In his affidavit, Chris said he allegedly delivered suitcases of money twice to Duterte in Davao from 2021 to 2022 upon Velasco’s instruction.

Prior to this, dismissed policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. said he delivered more than P2 billion in cash to Duterte and members of her family on the instructions of Velasco. The Vice President and other people named in the claims have denied the allegations.
Melvin Matibag, NBI director, said yesterday they will summon Chris to verify his account and supporting evidence.
He said Chris submitted an affidavit and photographs linking him to trips to Davao City in 2021 and 2022. His account could corroborate Gracioso’s allegations.
“He is one of the drivers mentioned as having accompanied Gracioso,” Matibag said in an interview over True FM.

The NBI chief said investigators would examine the witness’s photographs, social media posts and other possible evidence before making recommendations. He added the bureau would summon Chris for further questioning and ask whether he would agree to undergo a polygraph examination.
Matibag said the witness reportedly received at least P150,000 per delivery, but clarified that he had yet to personally review the affidavit.

Chris, who appeared before the NBI on Thursday, told reporters that he joined two trips to Davao, transporting an estimated 15 suitcases each time. He said their head driver told him the luggage contained a “small gift” for Duterte.
However, Chris admitted that he did not know what the suitcases contained and never saw the Vice President. He said he and the other drivers were left outside the destination.
Matibag said the new witness’s account appeared consistent with some details disclosed by Gracioso, but stressed the NBI would carefully validate the information before reaching conclusions.

The bureau also plans to invite Velasco and other people mentioned in the allegations to clarify their involvement. Matibag said immigration records indicated that Velasco was last reported to be in Japan, with investigators checking information that he may be in the Niseko area. — Mark Ernest Villeza

articles.title: Diokno: Concrete plan needed amid peso drop
articles.summary: Akbayan party-list Rep. Chel Diokno urged the Marcos administration to present a clear and concrete plan to address the peso’s continued depreciation and cushion its impact on ordinary families.

blocks.text: October 31, 2026 | 12:00am
House prosecutor and Akbayan Representative Chel Diokno delivers his oral arguments before the Senate impeachment court on July 15, 2026.
Ryan Baldemor / The Philippine STAR

MANILA, Philippines — Akbayan party-list Rep. Chel Diokno urged the Marcos administration to present a clear and concrete plan to address the peso’s continued depreciation and cushion its impact on ordinary families.

Diokno said it is important that public assurances are matched by decisive action and practical measures to manage the economic challenges and mitigate the effects of rising prices on household budgets.

“Apart from advice, what the people are waiting for is the government’s swift action to lessen the effects of continued increase in prices of basic goods and the weak value of the peso,” he said in a statement.
He stressed that families already struggling to make ends meet need clear answers on what the government will do to help them cope with rising living costs.
“The government must lay out clear, concrete measures to address these economic pressures and ease the burden on ordinary households,” Diokno said.

“Every time the peso weakens and prices rise, families can afford less with what they earn. The government must act to protect their purchasing power and ensure that basic necessities remain within reach,” he said.
The Philippine peso has fallen to historic levels of over P64 versus the US dollar.

articles.title: How tech can help Filipinos weather El Niño impact
articles.summary: From low-cost water filtration systems to biofertilizers and automated irrigation, Filipino-made technologies are offering practical solutions to water shortages and agricultural losses as the…

blocks.text: October 31, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — From low-cost water filtration systems to biofertilizers and automated irrigation, Filipino-made technologies are offering practical solutions to water shortages and agricultural losses as the country braces for the impact of a “super” El Niño.
The Department of Agriculture has reported P8.6 billion in crop losses, underscoring the need for measures to help farmers cope with prolonged dry conditions.
In response, Filipino innovators are developing homegrown technologies and practical solutions to help communities adapt to its effects.
Biochar filter
One such innovation is a biochar water filter developed by Sambali Beach Farm, a social enterprise in Zambales that uses charcoal recycled from discarded young coconuts, or buko.
The filtration system uses charcoal, cleaned sand and stones to filter water through a series of drums, making it suitable for drinking. The four-drum setup costs P4,800 and can be used for one year.
The enterprise has donated filtration systems to Aeta communities in Zambales, where water stations are scarce. Subdivision owners and farmers have also adopted the technology to reduce costs.

“Actually, we made this for disaster response, so local government units (LGUs) should have this,” Jeanet Delfierro, a community organizer at Sambali Beach Farm, said on the sidelines of the “Handa Pilipinas Luzon Leg” in Clark, Pampanga, an initiative of the Department of Science and Technology. “Whenever there are disasters, they can bring this to areas with no source of water.
“They can get water from the pump or the river and put it in there. It will be filtered and you don’t have to spend millions of pesos,” she added.
To demonstrate the filter’s effectiveness, Sambali Beach Farm uses it in its restaurant, where foreign visitors also drink the filtered water, Delfierro said.

The enterprise supports 500 households across the Zambales provincial capital of Iba and the towns of Botolan, Cabangan, Palauig and San Felipe. Delfierro hopes to secure more funding to expand its operations to other towns in the province.
Nutrio biofertilizer

Aside from addressing water shortages, the DOST is scaling up technologies to help farmers cope with El Niño through Project SARAI, or Smarter Approaches to Reinvigorate Agriculture as an Industry in the Philippines, which has received continuing appropriations of P600 million since 2025.
Among the technologies being promoted is Nutrio, a biofertilizer developed by researchers from the University of the Philippines Los Baños.
Made with microorganisms, the product helps crops such as sugarcane achieve better yields at a lower cost.
Marlon Gamboa, a farmer from Paniqui, Tarlac, took a chance on the biofertilizer two years ago at Ruby’s Farm to reduce his reliance on conventional urea fertilizer.
“More than 50 percent of the cost of the fertilizer will be lost if you use Nutrio,” Gamboa told reporters during a visit in July.

Nutrio is being tested in seven provinces, including Tarlac. In a commercial trial in Concepcion, farmers who used Nutrio alongside urea harvested 69.25 tons of sugarcane per hectare, 23 percent above the national average. The trial also generated an additional income of P72,755.

Each bag of Nutrio costs P350, an added expense that Gamboa acknowledged. However, he said the benefits have been substantial, with Ruby’s Farm now harvesting an average of 125 tons of cane per hectare per cropping season, up from 30 to 40 tons previously.
Irrigation system
To further improve production and reduce water waste, Gamboa also adopted an automated furrow irrigation system developed by Central Luzon State University (CLSU).
The P400,000 system regulates the amount and timing of irrigation water, helping farmers avoid unnecessary water use.

“We have two soil moisture sensors: the first (sensor) will dictate when you will water the soil… When the sugarcane has consumed 50 percent of the available soil moisture, that’s when irrigation will begin,” Marvin Cinense, director of CLSU’s Philippine-Sino Center for Agricultural Technology, said during a demonstration.
“We do not need to water the sugarcane often. The sub-sensor will determine when it stops. That means we are reducing the losses,” he added.
Promoting solutions
Despite the potential benefits of local innovations, getting the public to adopt them remains a challenge.

One example is the Department of Social Welfare and Development’s water filtration kit, suggested by President Marcos, which drew ridicule from some Filipinos amid discussions about collecting rainwater to address El Niño.
DOST Secretary Renato Solidum Jr. defended the kit, saying its specialized bucket can collect rainwater and filter out particles to make the water for drinking.

articles.title: 2-year delay on CCTV turnover at NAIA irks Dizon
articles.summary: Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon expressed dismay at the nearly two-year delay in the transfer of closed-circuit television control at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport.

blocks.text: October 31, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon expressed dismay at the nearly two-year delay in the transfer of closed-circuit television control at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport.

During an inspection at the NAIA Terminal 1 yesterday as Undas approaches, Dizon was frustrated at how the transfer of CCTV control from the Manila International Airport Authority (MIAA) to the New NAIA Infrastructure Corp. (NNIC) has been delayed, citing safety concerns.
“The problem here is there’s no single accountability. Our problem is simple, someone was robbed and you are all pointing fingers,” the Department of Transportation chief said.
“We’ve been fixing the transfer since last year. I want this turnover done immediately. So, we will only scold one and you will not point fingers. Nothing will happen to us,” he added.
Dizon ordered the MIAA to turn over the responsibility, authority, and operations of all CCTV cameras to NNIC by November.
He warned the involved officials that they will be fired should they not beat the deadline.
In addition, Dizon ordered NNIC to add more CCTV cameras in every corner of the terminal in order to ensure the safety of passengers.
The inspection was triggered after a French tourist was robbed of three high-value timepieces worth millions.
Dizon said – with the assistance of Sen. Raffy Tulfo and his staff – the suspect was identified and the items were retrieved.
Around 1.2 million passengers are expected to flock NAIA terminals from Oct. 27 to Nov. 4.
On the other hand, Dizon lauded the other improvements of the terminals such as a renovated arrival area and automated immigration gates.
He noted that all Filipinos can access e-gates aside from overseas Filipinos workers and foreigners in order to avoid long lines.
According to the MIAA, they will complete the turnover of the CCTV surveillance system to the NNIC within November.

The MIAA has already completed the final acceptance of the CCTV project, and initiated the necessary arrangements for its formal turnover to NNIC in accordance with the NAIA Public-Private Partnership Concession Agreement.

Meanwhile, the MIAA continues its CCTV repair and restoration efforts, in coordination with Abratique & Associates Philippines Inc., while maintaining appropriate security measures to protect passengers and other airport users. — Rudy Santos

articles.title: BAN Toxics warns of chemicals in Halloween toys
articles.summary: A watchdog group has warned consumers about hazardous chemicals found in Halloween toys and costumes, urging manufacturers and importers to comply with Philippine safety standards to protect children…

blocks.text: October 31, 2026 | 12:00am
Shoppers browse Halloween toys and costumes at Divisoria Market in Manila on October 30, 2026 as Filipinos prepare for Halloween celebrations.
Ryan Baldemor / The Philippine STAR

MANILA, Philippines — A watchdog group has warned consumers about hazardous chemicals found in Halloween toys and costumes, urging manufacturers and importers to comply with Philippine safety standards to protect children from toxic exposure.

In a statement released to Bulacan reporters, Thony Dizon, advocacy and campaign officer of BAN Toxics, cautioned the public against allowing toxic chemicals to turn trick-or-treating into a health hazard.

During a recent market monitoring and purchasing activity, BAN Toxics subjected various Halloween toys and costumes to chemical screening using a Vanta C Series HH XRF Analyzer. The tests detected lead content of up to 1,130 parts per million and cadmium levels of up to 160 ppm.

The group also reported that all the children’s Halloween items it monitored and inspected failed to meet the product labeling standards mandated by Republic Act 10620, or the Toy and Game Safety Labeling Act of 2013.

“Manufacturers and importers of these toys should comply with existing Philippine safety standards on chemical content and product labeling, which are mandatory to protect children from toxic exposure,” Dizon said.

He noted that the use of lead in the production and sale of toys is strictly prohibited under the Department of Environment and Natural Resources’ Administrative Order 2013-24, or the Chemical Control Order for Lead and Lead Compounds.

Republic Act 10620 also requires toy manufacturers to comply with labeling requirements, including the License to Operate number issued by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), age grading, cautionary statements and warnings, instructional literature, the manufacturer’s complete name and address, and the item model or Stock Keeping Unit number.
BAN Toxics urged the FDA and local government units to conduct post-market surveillance and confiscate unlabeled and unnotified toys and child care articles, including children’s Halloween products.

“Preventing the spread of unsafe children’s products in the market should be the core action not just of a single agency but a concerted effort by all stakeholders, including local government units and the general public,” the group said.

articles.title: Gas prices seen higher next week; rollback for diesel
articles.summary: Motorists should brace for higher gasoline prices next week as the escalating conflict in the Middle East continues to threaten critical oil supply.

blocks.text: October 31, 2026 | 12:00am
Gasoline prices are projected to rise by P2.90 to as high as P3.20 per liter. On the other hand, diesel prices could drop by P0.40 to P0.60 per liter next week.
The STAR / Walter Bollozos
MANILA, Philippines — Motorists should brace for higher gasoline prices next week as the escalating conflict in the Middle East continues to threaten critical oil supply.
The recent estimates are based on the four-day movements in the foreign exchange rate and the Mean of Platts Singapore, the regional benchmark for refined petroleum products in the Asia-Pacific.
Jetti Petroleum president Leo Bellas said oil prices remained supported by concerns over possible supply disruptions in the Middle East.

“Diesel and gasoline closely followed the movement of crude oil, which continues to be supported by concerns about energy supply disruptions in the Middle East as regional attacks continue and worries the US could strike Iran after next week’s US midterm elections,” he said.
He noted that hopes for a diplomatic breakthrough in the conflict helped limit a surge in prices.
“However, hopes for a breakthrough in the diplomatic efforts to end the eight-month-long conflict helped pare oil’s further rise,” Bellas added.
He said that improving fuel supply prospects helped unwind diesel and gasoline gains after China issued a fourth batch of fuel export quotas for gasoline, diesel and jet fuel.
He added that South Korea’s easing of diesel export restrictions helped offer additional relief for tight Asian and global markets.
Additional supply prospects were seen after Russia’s diesel and gasoline exports peaked amid the pause in Ukrainian refinery strikes.
“These factors have pressured diesel, reversing earlier gains,” Bellas added.
The final domestic pump price adjustments would still depend on the outcome of this week’s last trading day. The forecast does not yet account for week-on-week changes in freight costs.
The Department of Energy has mandated that all oil companies follow its prescribed maximum price increases, amid the ongoing national energy emergency.

articles.title: DepEd gains international recognition for improved PISA results
articles.summary: The Department of Education (DepEd) gained international recognition for its recent performance improvements in the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA).

blocks.text: October 31, 2026 | 12:00am
This file photo shows the Department of Education.
STAR / File
MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Education (DepEd) gained international recognition for its recent performance improvements in the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA).

Harvard Graduate School of Education dean Nonie Lesaux praised the Philippines for its 2025 PISA results, where the country emerged as the world’s fastest-improving nation in reading performance and ranked among the top improvers overall, significantly increasing scores across reading, mathematics and science.

Education Secretary Sonny Angara welcomed the commendation, emphasizing that external validation serves as a morale boost for the country’s teachers and learners while underscoring the urgency of compounding these early gains through systemic reforms.

“We see this as a clear mandate to work harder. Our goal is to ensure that every Filipino child is actually learning, comprehending and thriving,” Angara said during a forum organized by the Harvard Club of the Philippines Global at the Manila House Private Club in Bonifacio Global City.

The dialogue, attended by DepEd officials and Harvard alumni, focused on strategies to transform foundational learning, strengthen teacher competencies, utilize education-technology effectively and bridge persistent learning gaps.
Lesaux, an internationally recognized scholar in language and literacy development, shared insights closely aligned with DepEd’s ongoing structural interventions.
These include the flagship Academic Recovery and Accessible Learning (ARAL) Program, which has driven measurable gains in literacy and grade-readiness.

“When experts from institutions like Harvard point out that our PISA performance trends are moving in the right direction, it tells us that our teachers are delivering, our kids are catching up and our programs like ARAL are hitting the mark. But the real work lies in scaling these successes so that geography or background never dictates a child’s future,” he added.

articles.title: Stricter transport safety, security checks sought
articles.summary: Senate committee on public services chairman Sen. Raffy Tulfo has urged agencies to ensure the safety of millions of people expected to travel to their provinces during the Undas holiday, calling for…

blocks.text: October 31, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Senate committee on public services chairman Sen. Raffy Tulfo has urged agencies to ensure the safety of millions of people expected to travel to their provinces during the Undas holiday, calling for stricter inspections of public utility vehicles and tighter security at airports and seaports.
During a recent committee hearing, Tulfo directed the Land Transportation Office (LTO) to ensure that passenger buses are roadworthy before being allowed to operate.
Inspections should cover properly functioning brakes, worn-out tires and drug testing for drivers, while colorum buses should be prohibited from operating, he said.
“Even when it is not Undas, the LTO should still conduct regular inspections,” Tulfo said.
He also raised concerns about airport security, with more than 1.25 million passengers expected to travel during Undas 2026.

He cited the robbery of French national Anthony Boukhors, who lost luxury watches at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Terminal 1, where some closed-circuit television cameras were reportedly not operational.

Tulfo called for all CCTV cameras to be working before the holiday rush and for adequate security personnel to be deployed throughout airport premises to respond promptly to incidents and deter criminals.

The senator also urged the Maritime Industry Authority, Philippine Ports Authority and Philippine Coast Guard to ensure that vessels comply with safety standards before sailing, including sufficient life jackets, passenger capacity limits, proper cargo weight limits and accurate passenger manifests.
“No life should be lost due to negligence,” he stressed.
President Marcos orders safety measures
President Marcos has ordered government agencies to ensure the safety and convenience of Filipinos traveling to their provinces and visiting cemeteries to observe All Saints’ Day and All Souls’ Day.

“This Undas, many of our fellow Filipinos will go home to their respective provinces and visit cemeteries to remember and pray for their loved ones. We are ensuring that their travel and visit will be safe, smooth, and convenient,” Marcos said in a video message on Friday.
According to the Parañaque Integrated Terminal Exchange (PITX), more than one million passengers have passed through the landport ahead of the Undas weekend.
Between Oct. 25 and 29, the terminal recorded 931,225 passengers. Another 137,807 were added as of 5 p.m. on Friday, for a total of 1,069,032.
PITX projects 1.9 million passengers from Oct. 25 to Nov. 4, down from the 2.1 million recorded last year.
The President said the government was ensuring that Filipinos would have safe, orderly and convenient trips during the observance.

The Maritime Industry Authority has issued relaxation orders and special permits allowing flexible shipping schedules and additional ferry trips from Oct. 29 to Nov. 3 to accommodate increased passenger demand on selected routes.

Likewise, the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board has also issued more than 1,000 special permits for additional bus trips, while the Department of Transportation and its attached agencies are inspecting airports, seaports and bus terminals.
Marcos said 24-hour help desks are available at major transport terminals from Oct. 29 to Nov. 3.
Airport immigration counters will also have enough personnel on duty from Oct. 30 to Nov. 3 to prevent long lines, with digital systems such as eGates to be used to speed up processing.
He also directed the Philippine National Police (PNP) to deploy personnel to cemeteries and columbaria to maintain peace and order.

In response, the PNP has tightened security at cemeteries, memorial parks and transport hubs nationwide, deploying more than 141,000 police officers and force multipliers to secure 5,311 cemeteries and columbaria, major thoroughfares, transportation hubs, places of worship, tourist destinations and other areas where people are expected to gather.

“We will ensure that our personnel remain visible, approachable, and ready to respond to every request for assistance, especially from children, senior citizens and other vulnerable individuals,” PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. said.
The PNP will remain on full alert until Nov. 3.
Church: Treat ashes with respect
As Filipinos prepare to visit their departed loved ones, Catholic Church officials reminded the public to treat cremated remains with respect and follow Church guidelines on their proper disposition.

Taytay, Palawan Bishop Broderick Pabillo warned against taking portions of a loved one’s ashes to make necklaces or other personal mementos, saying families should respect the integrity of the remains.
“We should respect the integrity of the deceased… ‘I’ll take some parts of the ashes’ – that’s not right. It’s like we’re cutting parts of the body,” Pabillo said in an interview with Radyo Veritas.

He encouraged families visiting cemeteries on Nov. 1, which falls on a Sunday this year, to pray and attend mass together, saying the observance also offers an opportunity for families and relatives to reunite.
“I hope we can strengthen this even more through our collective prayers, especially this year, Nov. 1 is a Sunday, let’s go to church,” he said.
The Archdiocese of Manila has also issued guidelines on the proper treatment of cremated remains as part of the observance of All Saints’ Day and All Souls’ Day.
In Circular 2026-100, the Archdiocesan Liturgical Commission provided prayers for the departed in English and Filipino that may be used at home or when visiting cemeteries and columbaria.

The guidelines aim to deepen the faithful’s understanding of Church teachings and foster respect for the remains of departed loved ones in keeping with Christian belief. — Bella Cariaso, Emmanuel Tupas, EJ Macababbad

articles.title: Russian society being ‘systematically crushed’ says Novaya Gazeta as newspaper announces closure
articles.summary: Independent outlet, whose former editor Dmitry Muratov won Nobel prize, cites intolerable pressure from authorities

blocks.text: Novaya Gazeta, one of Russia’s best-known independent media outlets, has announced it will permanently close next month. The newspaper, whose former editor-in-chief Dmitry Muratov won the Nobel peace prize in 2021, cited intolerable pressure, including being stripped of its newsroom, its donation platforms and its legal right to publish.
“This is not just our own story; it is the story of a country and a society that are being systematically crushed,” wrote its editor-in-chief, Sergei Sokolov, on the newspaper’s website.

Launched in the 1990s and for many years partly funded by the late Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev, Novaya made its name through dogged, long-form reporting on corruption, rights abuses and social issues. Over the years, six of its journalists have been assassinated, including Anna Politkovskaya, who was gunned down in the stairwell of her Moscow apartment block in 2006.

While Novaya always swam against a tide of repression, the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 made independent reporting almost impossible and decimated the Russian media landscape. Novaya was one of the last critical voices still operating from inside the country.

“For nearly five years of ***, we managed to keep working while being completely encircled by the security services. Now it’s over. We have found ourselves in a ‘kill zone’,” wrote Sokolov. The stars were used in place of the word “war”, as under Russian law, journalists must refer to the war in Ukraine as a “special military operation” or face consequences.

blocks.caption: Sergei Sokolov, the Novaya Gazeta editor-in-chief.  Photograph: Igor Ivanko/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: The newspaper’s first response to the invasion was to put out a special bilingual Russian-Ukrainian edition in the days after Vladimir Putin launched the invasion. It described the war as “madness” on its front page. Soon after, the Kremlin implemented draconian new censorship laws, which forced media outlets to publish only the Russian official narrative about the conflict.

“We said it’s not journalism and we’re not going to do that,” said Nadezhda Prusenkova, the head of Novaya’s press service. The newspaper published blank white spaces instead of euphemisms and false information, to provide a visible reminder of the censorship laws.

By the end of March 2022, Novaya decided to stop publishing its print edition altogether, but the threats and pressure only increased. In April that year, Muratov was doused with red paint while on a train, an attack that damaged his eyesight and that US officials say was carried out on the orders of Russian intelligence agencies. In September that year, the newspaper’s official licence was taken away and soon after their website was blocked in Russia.

Novaya’s journalists, long used to operating in a hostile environment, found ways to circumvent the bans. Many left Russia, and a number of exiled former employees set up Novaya Gazeta Europe, a legally distinct outlet. Muratov and a core team stayed behind and continued to publish a series of magazines with a print run of 999 copies, taking advantage of a law that means magazines with under 1,000 copies do not require an official licence. Novaya’s website continued running, too, although the Russian state hit the outlet with various new legal threats.

“The fact Novaya kept working for this four and a half years after everything that happened was a miracle, but it was not just a miracle, it was also the daily choice of people who continued to go to work even when it was very scary,” said Elena Kostyuchenko, a former Novaya journalist who spent 17 years at the newspaper. “Today I feel very inspired by my colleagues, but also very painful and sad for them, and for all of us.”
after newsletter promotion

In recent months, Prusenkova said the pressure had become intolerable. In April, the journalist Oleg Roldugin was arrested and charged with “unlawful access to computerised information”. He is under house arrest awaiting trial and last month Sokolov’s home was searched as part of the case.

This month, the newspaper’s landlords informed Novaya staff that they must vacate their longstanding office premises in central Moscow by 9 November. The newsroom has been the hub of the newspaper for decades and houses a memorial museum to Politkovskaya in the former office of the murdered journalist. Prusenkova said the exhibits would be taken down and put into storage, for now.

On top of the eviction notice, all the outlet’s donation platforms have been shut down, leaving the paper without any source of funding. The court case, combined with the eviction and the lack of funds, gave the newspaper no choice but to close, said staff.

“Sometimes it happens that your enemies win. At this moment in time, it seems like they have won, and we have no options left,” said Prusenkova. But she said it was probable Novaya’s journalists would try to find some way to continue their work. “After all, we don’t know how to do anything else,” she said.

articles.title: US tech stocks see sharp falls over AI cost fears
articles.summary: Shares in Intel have continued to fall while the tech-heavy Nasdaq opens at its lowest level in more than two months.

blocks.text: US stocks have continued to slide as concerns continue to intensify over the increasing costs of the artificial intelligence (AI) build out.

Shares in Intel continued their overnight slide into early trading on Friday, falling as much as 30% after the chip maker warned of a weaker computer market even as it plans to increase spending on AI.
Amazon shares fell as far as 6% before recovering after its reported earnings on Thursday evening fell short of investors' expectations.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock exchange opened on Friday at its lowest level in more than two months, down 2.5%, as other tech stocks including Reddit and Roblox continued to fall.
The losses follow the value of Google owner Alphabet plunging by more than $500bn on Thursday after it revealed its own AI summaries were affecting its core search advertising revenue.
Alphabet stock continued to fall in early trading, down 1% after Thursday's massive slide.
The bigger losses on Friday were elsewhere, with Intel on track to lose more than $130bn in value after its earnings update rattled investors.
On Thursday, Intel's finance chief David Zinsner said the firm did not expect to bring in more cash than it spent this year, and forecast lower-than-expected revenue for its fourth quarter.
"Looking ahead, we see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," he said in the chip maker's third quarter earnings report.
In the earnings call, he said the firm had significantly ramped up investment in equipment in the third quarter and expected that to be "even more significant" in the following three months.
Reddit stock was down by 26%, after the social media platform revealed weaker-than-expected daily user figures and warned that Google's growing AI-driven search was hurting referral traffic.
Stock in online game platform Roblox also fell, down by nearly 20%, as its daily active user numbers dropped.
Several major tech firms have reported earnings this week, including Microsoft, and analysts said there were questions about the payout from the huge investments in AI.
Chris Low, from investment management firm FHN Financial, said the bulk of what was happening in the stock market was in reaction to some of the biggest tech players such as Amazon and Google.
He told Reuters the companies were "showing some pretty significant growing pains as they aggressively pursue the AI build-out".
"The thinking is that these signs suggest that the entire sector is going to slow down."
