articles.title: Yes, Halloween candy is expensive this year — but some sweets are scarier than others
articles.summary: Candy prices have climbed steadily over the past six years, according to Statistics Canada inflation numbers. But some treats are trickier than others. We break down which candies got more expensive…

image.caption: Halloween candy is displayed in a grocery store in Carmel, Ind., in October 2025. Candy prices have climbed steadily over the past six years, according to Statistics Canada monthly inflation numbers, rising 28 per cent since 2020. (Michael Conroy/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: A haunted house, but it's just your grocery bill after buying Halloween candy this year.

If you're feeling spooked stocking up for trick-or-treaters, you're not alone. The price of confectionery, which includes candy, has climbed steadily over the past six years, according to Statistics Canada monthly inflation numbers, rising 28 per cent since January 2020.

That's about four percentage points higher than the overall inflation rate for all consumer items during that time period. And while confectionery prices last month did dip slightly compared to September 2025, overall, some Canadian consumers are still experiencing sticker shock.

"Apparently Halloween candy is nearly $30 per box this year??" one person wrote on X last week, along with a photo of a store display of packages of 100 candy bars that were on sale for $13.99, but that are regularly $27.99 — a price CBC News confirmed at several Canadian retail locations, including Calgary Co-op and Save-On-Foods.
"I'm in Canada, and normally you could find a sale where the 100 packs of mini chocolates would go on sale for $10. The cheapest I found was $12," another consumer posted on Reddit Tuesday.
"Given the prices of the traditional Halloween candy, I went full size."

Still, some treats are trickier than others. And new data from the Agri-Food Analytics Lab at Dalhousie University in Halifax suggests that the treat with the biggest price hike this year isn't actually sweet, but salty.

The average price of chips and savoury snacks in October jumped about 18 per cent compared to last year, the data states. A pack of 40 small bags cost, on average, between $12.97 and $12.99 — about $2 more compared to 2025.

The October data provided to CBC News out of Dalhousie comes from the lab's review of grocery and pharmacy flyers in Vancouver, Calgary, Toronto, Montreal and Halifax, supplemented by online retail listings. It doesn't include tax or loyalty rewards.

September confectionery data from Statistics Canada — the most recent available — shows that even though prices have increased steadily since 2020, they are down 2.9 per cent this year, relative to September last year.

"Last year, we had the impact of the tariffs on sugar and confectionery, which is a big part of the reason prices were up dramatically [in 2025]," Michael von Massow, a food agriculture professor at Ontario's University of Guelph, told CBC News.
"Except for things like potato chips, which have no sugar or chocolate."
Chocolate levels out, thanks to sales

According to the Agri-Food Analytics Lab's October data, gummy candies (like Sour Patch Kids) were next on the list of price increases, with the price of a box of 90 sweets up 8.4 per cent compared to last October, followed by packs of chewy candies (like Skittles and Starburst), up about 6.5 per cent.
On the bright side, the price of pressed-sugar candies like Rockets was essentially unchanged.

The same went for boxes of chocolate treats, which had jumped as much as 30 per cent earlier in October, but have since levelled back out thanks to last-minute flyer sales, notes Sylvain Charlebois, the director of the Agri-Food Analytics Lab.

Cocoa prices have more than doubled over the past few years due to poor weather and disease in West Africa, which supplies more than 70 per cent of the world’s cocoa, according to The Associated Press.

items: Inflation rises to 3.1% in September, as fuel prices push higher: StatsCan
Are you being tricked by your treats? Some Halloween candy multipacks have shrunk in size, but not in price

blocks.text: A quick search of Toronto stores on Thursday showed a pack of 100 Nestlé assorted mini bars and candies on sale for $13.99 at Food Basics, Metro and Shoppers Drug Mart, and $15 at Loblaws — overall savings of about $9.

In Montreal, a bag of 100 Hershey assorted mini chocolate bars was on sale for $15.99 at Metro, down from $21.99. In Vancouver, the same bag was on sale for $11 at Loblaws, down from $20. No Frills in Dartmouth, N.S., had the item for $12.99, down from $18.99.
In other words, you can breathe a sigh of relief if you're just here for the peanut butter cups.
Still, watch out for shrinkflation, cautions Charlebois.

The tactic where companies quietly reduce the weight or volume of a product, but not the price, affected Halloween candy last year, when CBC News discovered two major candy makers had reduced the weight of several Halloween chocolate bar variety packs by as much as almost 17 per cent.
"Package size matters as much as the sticker price. A cheaper bag isn't necessarily a better deal if it contains fewer treats," he told CBC News.
Is chocolate way more expensive than it used to be?
Is it the candy, or everything else?
A few new reports from the U.S. also show rising Halloween candy prices — and sluggish sales.

U.S. candy prices have been climbing faster than inflation for several years. As of September, candy and gum prices were up 44 per cent over a five-year period, according to government data reported by The Associated Press.

In the U.S., the items that saw the biggest price increases compared to 2025 were Mondelez sour gummy candy variety packs (up about 40 per cent), followed by five different types of Hershey variety packs, including both chocolate and non-chocolate bundles, according to an analysis by Groundwork Collaborative.
Halloween candy is displayed for sale at a Giant grocery store on Oct. 22 in Dundalk, Md. (Stephanie Scarbrough/The Associated Press)

And U.S. Halloween candy sales fell 6.7 per cent in the month ended Oct. 17 compared to the same period last year, according to NielsenIQ, a market research firm. That wasn't necessarily because candy is more expensive, but because, well, everything is.

"I think what you're seeing now is a consumer that's spending so much additional money on fuel and housing and clothing and food," Chris Costagli, a vice-president of food thought leadership at NielsenIQ, told The Associated Press.
On Thursday, chocolate maker Hershey also warned that the rising cost of living might be spooking U.S. customers, rather than candy prices themselves.
That sentiment was echoed by some Canadian consumers on Reddit. Some posted in a Halifax subreddit that they didn't think candy prices were actually that bad this year.
"It's not the candy for us, it's everything else," one person commented.
"Sale prices are actually the best I've seen in a while," another person wrote in a subreddit for Burlington, Ont., last week.

"Regular price, the candy is absolutely ridiculous, I agree. But I've managed to buy about 300 pieces plus probably 40-50 full sized bars for, spitballing, around $100? I think even a little under that."
How Halloween became not just the spooky, but spendy, season

articles.title: Alaska Senate candidate denies knowing about alleged plot to put two Dan Sullivans on ballot
articles.summary: Dan S Sullivan, the incumbent Republican senator running for re-election, and allies have accused the Democrats of trying to confuse voters by recruiting Dan J Sullivan to also stand in the race.

blocks.text: Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola has denied she knew anything about an alleged "scheme" that led to two men named Dan Sullivan standing in the Alaska Senate race.

The denial comes as the Trump administration continues to escalate a criminal investigation into the matter, according to US media. The Republican governor of the state ordered an official inquiry earlier this week.
Dan S Sullivan, the incumbent Republican senator running for re-election, and allies have accused the Democrats of trying to confuse voters.
The Alaska race is considered by analysts to be one of the tightest of the upcoming US midterm elections, which will decide which party controls Congress.

"I just want to clear the air," Peltola said while speaking to voters on Thursday. "I knew nothing about any other candidate on the ballot except for me and the incumbent. That is all I have ever known about. I am not interested in tricking voters."

Both Dan Sullivans have been running for the open Senate seat for some time. Still, controversy erupted earlier this week when The New York Times, external reported that Peltola's team worked with people who tried to recruit spoiler candidates in the Senate race.

The Times's report alleged that people connected to Peltola's campaign, as well as senior aides at the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC), worked to try to recruit Dan J Sullivan, a retired teacher who lives in a remote fishing village, to stand in the Senate race.

The paper said it had seen text messages and interviewed 12 people who participated in or were told of the plan, or were would-be candidates who the team tried to recruit. The BBC has not independently verified the reporting.
The Peltola campaign has denied those reports and Sullivan has denied any links to the campaign.
But those denials have not stopped the US Department of Justice and Republicans from attacking Peltola.

The justice department has begun issuing subpoenas targeting Democratic officials allegedly connected to the effort to recruit Dan J Sullivan to be on the Alaska ballot, according to CBS News, the BBC's US news partner.
No charges have been filed as of Friday morning.

The Trump administration filed a federal lawsuit last week aimed at preventing the certification of the result if the Trump-backed Sullivan loses, arguing that the presence of both of them on the ballot could confuse voters.

On Wednesday, the justice department amended its lawsuit to include the reporting by the Times, citing significant sections of the story as well as Governor Mike Dunleavy's announcement of an investigation.

The legal action comes days before voters across the US head to the polls. This race in Alaska is among the closest-watched in the country, as it could be the deciding factor in who controls the Senate.
The non-partisan Cook Political Report currently classifies the race as a toss-up.

articles.title: US inmate Christa Pike says she woke up 'confused and in pain' after failed execution
articles.summary: It is Pike's first public statement since she survived an execution attempt by lethal injection in September.

blocks.text: US death row inmate Christa Pike has released her first public statement since her botched execution in September.
"There hasn't been a moment since that night when I haven't been in pain," she said in a statement released by her legal team on social media on Friday.
"My body hurts. My arms hurt. My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak. And the pain isn't just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul."
Pike, 50, was discharged from hospital at the end of last month after surviving two lethal injections of the drug pentobarbital, which left her in a critical condition.
She has since been sent back to the prison where she has spent the last 30 years for murdering Colleen Slemmer in 1995.
Pike is thought to be the only person to have survived an execution attempt by lethal injection.
Her lawyers previously said she had suffered from pneumonia following the attempted execution, had significant swelling on her arms and was also unable to swallow.
"I am recovering, and I know that I am getting stronger," she said in her statement on Friday. "But healing is not the same as being okay."
Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer, whom they had met at a job training camp for low-income young people.
Shipp was spared the death penalty because he was not legally an adult when the crime was committed. He remains in prison.

articles.title: Ombudsman suspends Bulacan DPWH engineers over P188M flood control projects
articles.summary: The Office of the Ombudsman has ordered the preventive suspension of five engineers of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Bulacan First District Engineering Office for six months.

blocks.text: The Office of the Ombudsman has ordered the preventive suspension of five engineers of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Bulacan First District Engineering Office for six months.
This is in light of the ongoing investigation into their alleged involvement in the anomalous P188 million worth of flood control projects in Baliuag, Bulacan.

The preventive suspension order covered DPWH project engineers Irene Ontingco, Kevin Geronimo, John Michael Ramos, Bernardo Villafuerte, and Michelle Cruz, pending the resolution of administrative cases against them alleging grave misconduct, serious dishonesty, and gross neglect of duty in connection with the construction of reinforced concrete slope revetments in Barangays Piel, San Roque, and Sulivan in Baliuag, Bulacan.

"To facilitate the implementation of the contracts and the disbursement of public funds, complainant maintains that respondents falsified documents relating to contract implementation, inspection, acceptance, billing and payment to create the false impression that the contractual and legal prerequisites had been satisfied," the order read.

“The Ombudsman found sufficient grounds to believe that the allegations against the respondents were supported by strong evidence at this stage of the proceedings. Allowing the respondents to remain in their positions could prejudice the ongoing investigation, particularly as they may have access to or custody of documents and other evidence relevant to the case,” the Ombudsman added.

The administrative complaint filed against the respondents by Ombudsman prosecutors alleged that they falsified documents related to the implementation, inspection, acceptance, billing, and payment of the projects to make it appear that contractual and legal requirements had been complied with.

“The preventive suspension was likewise deemed necessary to preserve evidence and prevent possible further malfeasance or misfeasance in office while the administrative proceedings are ongoing,” the Ombudsman added.

Also included in the administrative complaint are former Bulacan officer-in-charge district engineer Brice Ericson Hernandez, former assistant district engineer Jaypee Mendoza, former contract claims unit head Arjay Domasig, and former accountant Juanito Mendoza, who are already in jail over malversation and graft cases involving the P92.8 million Pandi, Bulacan flood control project.
However, the preventive suspension for those already in jail has been rendered moot after they have been separated from service.
The prayer for the preventive suspension of DPWH engineer Norberto Santos and administrative officer Floralyn Simbulan was likewise rendered moot following their detention in Quezon City and Bulacan.

Meanwhile, DPWH former administrative officer Evelyn De Jesus and former engineer Ernesto Galang have already retired from service, while former materials engineer Vicente Calderon and former project engineer Merg Jaron Laus have resigned in 2026, rendering the suspension against them moot as well.
Apart from the administrative case, the respondents also face criminal complaints with the Office of the Ombudsman.
GMA News Online has reached out to DPWH Region 3 for comment and will publish it as soon as it is made available.—LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Montreal police officer allegedly deleted domestic violence video, investigation launched
articles.summary: According to Radio-Canada, a Montreal police officer at Station 39 allegedly deleted video evidence provided in 2025 by a woman who was a victim of domestic violence.

image.caption: On June 12, and in light of an internal investigation into racists acts committed by police officers, management at the SPVM disarmed 16 officers, suspended two, assigned three to administrative duties and relocated 11. By mid-August, police said four officers had been suspended. (Ivanoh Demers/Radi

blocks.text: Montreal·New
According to Radio-Canada, a Montreal police officer at Station 39 allegedly deleted video evidence provided in 2025 by a woman who was a victim of domestic violence.
Radio-Canada is reporting that an officer allegedly destroyed evidence in domestic violence case
Montreal police say the Quebec Crown prosecution's office is investigating an officer alleged to have committed misconduct and obstruction involving a case of domestic violence in 2025.
In a statement, police said the report surfaced during the investigation into Station 39 in Montréal-Nord, which has been at the centre of a major racism scandal since June.
Police also said the complaint originated within the police force.

The statement from police didn't include many more details, but Radio-Canada learned that the officer is facing allegations of destroying a video on the smartphone of a woman who was a victim of domestic violence.
According to Radio-Canada, a police duo — one man and one woman — responded to a residence in Montréal-Nord following an emergency call from a woman saying she had been a victim of domestic violence.

The alleged victim reportedly opened her phone to give video evidence of the abuse to the officers. As the male officer watched the video, he reportedly recognized the alleged aggressor and deleted the video in front of his police partner. She then later reported the actions of the officer to two sergeants on duty.
Radio-Canada learned that female officer had to escalate her concerns within the SPVM because her concerns were ignored by her supervisors.
In its news release, the Service de police de la Ville de Montréal (SPVM) said the investigation into the officer is ongoing and that they have reassigned the officer to administrative tasks.
He will not hold a public-facing role until the investigation ends, the SPVM said.

items: 2 Montreal police officers accused of humiliating acts, including urinating on homeless people

blocks.text: "My confidence has been shaken by several police officers who cast a shadow — a serious shadow — on the exceptional work of other officers," said Mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada.

In a separate case, Montreal police have also said that an officer from Station 21 in downtown Montreal has been suspended for alleged racist and discriminatory acts related to the probe regarding Station 39.
Montreal police chief Fady Dagher will provide an update this afternoon on the allegations surrounding the Station 39 investigation.
"The police chief has a lot of explaining to do to the citizens of Montreal today, with yet another incident having just occured," said Martinez Ferrada.
"He has a duty to restore trust with the public, and I expect that to be his focus in the coming days."

items: Did a lack of veteran oversight set the stage for a Montreal police scandal?

blocks.text: Yves Francoeur, the president of the Fraternité des policiers et policières de Montréal, the union representing police officers in Montreal, told Radio-Canada it would not comment until they review the entire file.
In June, a 16-member patrol unit from Station 39 was suspended following allegations of discrimination and misconduct.
Those allegations included cutting locs from people's hair during police interventions and collecting them as trophies.
With files from Radio-Canada

articles.title: Bayern Munich's Kenya friendly highlights Africa's growing pull for global sport
articles.summary: Bayern Munich are to open Nairobi's new Raila Odinga International Stadium against Ajax as Kenya prepares for AFCON 2027. The match highlights Africa's growing sports ambitions — and questions over…

image.caption: Bayern Munich and Ajax will play the game that opens the new 60,000-seater stadium in NairobiImage: Simon Maina/AFP

blocks.text: Bundesliga champions Bayern Munich are to travel to Nairobi, Kenya during the winter break to play a friendly that opens the newly finished Raila Odinga International Stadium in the capital city. The German side will face Ajax Amsterdam as the game acts as part of the country's preparations for the 2027 African Cup of Nations (AFCON), which will be held in Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania next summer.

"Bayern has millions of fantastic fans in Africa with whom we feel a close connection – it's a continent with a huge passion for football," Rouven Kasper, Bayern board member for marketing and sales, said in a club statement.
"We will be making a further contribution to raising the profile of the Bundesliga and are very much looking forward to this special event."
Why are global sports rushing to invest in Africa?

The news is just the latest venture into global sports investing in Africa. Earlier this month, Formula 1 announced it was returning to the continent after Rwanda secured the rights for a deal from the early 2030s onwards. In September, World Athletics revealed Nairobi would host the World Championships in 2029. It will be the first time the event has been held in Africa.

Simon Chadwick, a business management and program director at the African School of Economics, believes that over the last two decades the professionalization and industrialization of sports has begun to emerge in Africa.

"Countries like Rwanda, Kenya, Morocco and obviously, South Africa, if we go back to the last decade of the previous century, have increasingly begun to deploy sport as a policy instrument," Chadwick told DW, adding Senegal and Egypt to the list.
"There are these image and reputational benefits which very often are bundled up as soft power. It's about attractiveness and appeal and engagement," said Chadwick.

"It's almost like a kind of professionalization, industrialization and politicization of sport that we're seeing elsewhere in the world has now arrived in Africa. We are seeing a much greater sense of kind of self-determination within Africa to do this," he added.
"This is not just about sport. It is also about diplomacy and bilateral trade, but also about the broader economic and industrial context within which sport sits."

blocks.caption: Football has boomed in Morocco, as the development of stadiums like the Prince Moulay Abdellah stadium prove.Image: Emre Asikci/Anadolu/picture alliance

blocks.text: A coup for Kenya sport, but at what cost?

For Kenya specifically, the building of the stadium is in line with the housing and sports infrastructural development that has been so heavily promoted under President William Ruto. Hosting this game is a symbol of the development currently happening in Nairobi.

"The bigger picture is that Nairobi now is positioning itself as a as an alternative sports venue," Richard Wanjohi, Editorial and Research Lead at the African Sports and Creative Institute (ASCI), told DW.

"I think we have seen what Kigali has done over the last number of years. For us to then come back into this conversation as a major city that can host such an event, it's huge. A few weeks later, we'll have the rugby sevens series again and then ultimately, the Africa Cup of Nations in July."
Marathon G.O.A.T Eliud Kipchoge
Chadwick believes that unlike Rwanda, Kenya's relative stability and pre-existing tourist industry allows for a more natural development of sports investment.
"This is not Kenya trying to build a tourism industry through an engagement in sport. I think it's an extension of what Kenya has been doing for a number of years through sport."
Combined with being a multi-sport country - athletics, rugby, football, volleyball – Wanjohi believes Kenya is ready to make the most of that performance on the field or track.

"It's about time that we also host the world and show them that we can do this from a hosting perspective, but also from developing infrastructure that is ready to host such sports events," Wanjohi said.

"It's beyond just saying that we have the talent that is already in the sport, but it's saying that we have the infrastructure, we have the skills, we have the capability to host this as any other African, if not global nation."

blocks.caption: William Ruto (right) is a huge sports fan, in particular football, making his investment into a brand new stadium in Nairobi not very surprisingImage: Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images/AFP

blocks.text: Sporting development not free of criticism

However, Ruto's government has been criticized over taxation, unemployment and its handling of dissent. Given that this stadium cost approximately €375 million ($418 million), it is perhaps no surprise that questions are being asked about the decision to invest in major sports infrastructure.

"People are asking, we are a struggling economy. There are a lot of other issues that could be addressed, like the education sector, health and all that. How did we get that money and be able to make that provision? Also interestingly, is that there's an appearance fee that is going to be paid to both Bayern and Ajax," said Wanjohi, who added there was also some frustration that the opening game was not given to local teams or even the national side.
Ultimately, the timing of this also matters. While many sports fans in the country are excited, others are critical.

"The government knows that this is almost like a campaign tool. We have an election coming up in August next year so the government or the president of the day obviously wants to use as much leverage of such an event to milk it for all it's worth," Wanjohi added.
"So the two different schools of thought are: It's a good thing to have, but at what cost are we doing it at and is it in the public interest as well?"
The proof will be in what the legacy of events like Bayern Munich's friendly in Nairobi brings Kenyan football. The feeling in late 2026 though, is largely optimistic.

"I guess the acid test is that many African nations carry with them the baggage from the past that this is just trophy asset investment that is ultimately going to create white, white elephant infrastructure," Chadwick said.
"But having spoken to people in Kenyan sport, in the industry itself, it seems to me that there is a genuine appetite for sports to become a genuine and legitimate driver of economic activity."
Janek Speight contributed reporting for this article.

articles.title: Russian independent paper Novaya Gazeta finally forced to close its doors
articles.summary: 'The newspaper no longer exists. The Russian authorities and the Russian security services have forced our editorial team to cease its operations,' says the publication. Its final issue will be…

blocks.text: A man stands outside the office of the independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta during a reported search by security services as part of an unspecified investigation, in Moscow, Russia, on April 9, 2026.
Ramil Sitdikov/Reuters

'The newspaper no longer exists. The Russian authorities and the Russian security services have forced our editorial team to cease its operations,' says the publication. Its final issue will be published on November 9.

items: Novaya Gazeta, an independent Russian newspaper, is ceasing operations due to state pressure, including the prosecution of a senior editor and the revocation of financial support.

The publication, founded in 1993 with ties to Mikhail Gorbachev, has faced increasing censorship and restrictions since the onset of the Ukraine war in 2022, leading to the halt of its print edition and the blocking of its website.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MOSCOW, Russia – The Russian independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta said on Friday, October 30, that it was winding up its remaining operations after a campaign of state pressure in which a senior editor has been prosecuted and its financial support and premises have been taken away.
“We have been killed,” the publication, set up with money from the Nobel Peace Prize of the last Soviet leader, Mikhail Gorbachev, said in a statement.
The paper halted its print edition inside Russia in 2022, but had continued to produce online content and operate from its office in central Moscow.

“On November 9, we will turn off the lights in the home where we have lived for 30 years, shut down our servers, and leave,” it said. “The newspaper no longer exists. The Russian authorities and the Russian security services have forced our editorial team to cease its operations.”
There was no immediate comment from the authorities, which had designated the publication a “foreign agent.”

But the Kremlin — which accuses foreign intelligence services of trying to stir up discontent inside Russian society — has said in the past that some censorship is necessary at a time when Russia is locked in what it describes as an existential struggle with the West over Ukraine.

The prominent war blogger Rybar offered a taste of how the publication is seen in some official circles, reposting a diatribe that accused Novaya Gazeta of systematically promoting an anti-Russian narrative and of relishing the difficulties faced by the Russian state.

Founded in 1993 in line with Gorbachev’s vision of “glasnost” or openness, Novaya Gazeta (“New Newspaper”) became one of Russia’s most influential newspapers and defenders of democracy with its investigations into corruption and critical coverage of Russian politics.

Dmitry Muratov, its co-founder and long-time editor-in-chief, shared the 2021 Nobel Peace Prize, dedicating it to six colleagues who had been killed because of their work, including the investigative journalist Anna Politkovskaya, who wrote about Moscow’s wars in the restive Chechnya region.

Like other media outlets not run by the state but critical of it, Novaya Gazeta came under increasing pressure after Russia launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in 2022. Sweeping censorship rules were introduced that mandated long jail terms for “discrediting” the Russian army or disseminating what the authorities deem to be fake news.

“Since the start of the ‘special military operation’ in Ukraine and the introduction of criminal charges for ‘discrediting the Russian army’, we cannot report on the most critical and tragic events of our time,” the newspaper said. “Censorship applies to virtually every sphere of civic life.”

Many of its own journalists and those from other outlets had fled Russia in 2022, it added. Some of its former employees began a separate Latvian-based print and online publication called Novaya Gazeta Europe, which the Moscow authorities designated an “undesirable organisation,” effectively banning it within Russia. It will continue to operate.

Inside Russia, Novaya Gazeta noted that its website had been blocked, its print license revoked and its presses seized, and that one of its editors, Oleg Roldugin, was under house arrest awaiting trial on allegations that he misused personal data, an offence that carries a prison term of up to 10 years.
Its offices in central Moscow — from which it is now being evicted — have also been searched by the authorities, and the home of Sergei Sokolov, its editor-in-chief, was also searched this month.
“We carried on as long as we could,” Novaya Gazeta said in its farewell statement. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Spain transport minister says he won't resign over high-speed rail disaster
articles.summary: Óscar Puente has been facing calls to resign after two high-speed trains collided earlier in the week, killing at least 69 people.

blocks.text: Spain's transport minister says he won't resign over the high-speed rail collision that has left at least 69 people dead.
Óscar Puente told a news conference in Madrid he had "nothing to hide" while repeating the government's vow to get to the bottom of the disaster, saying many questions needed to be answered.
"My duty right now is not to talk about whether I should remain in my position, but to resolve the problem," Puente said.

The transport minister has been facing calls to step down in the aftermath of the tragedy, including from political rivals, a trade union and demonstrators who protested outside the transport ministry on Wednesday night.

Dozens were killed and many more injured when a state-operated Renfe high-speed train smashed into the back of another stationary train operated by the Iryo company near the town of Urda, in the central Toledo province, on Wednesday morning.

A preliminary report released by transport investigators late on Thursday found the Renfe train was travelling between 160km/h (99.4mph) and 200km/h when the collision occurred, causing its front carriage to become embedded in the tail of the stationary train.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said earlier on Friday that public trust in Spain's high-speed rail network had been broken and repeated it was "unacceptable" that there had been two similar tragedies within a year.
In January a collision on the same Madrid-Seville route killed 46 people in Adamuz in southern Spain.
Wednesday's tragedy was one of the worst rail disasters in Europe's modern history, and Spain's worst crash since 2013.
Puente said on Wednesday a computer failure at about 08:30 that morning led to the initial halt of six moving trains, including the two trains that subsequently collided.
Leaked audio recordings published in Spanish media revealed conversations between train drivers and a control centre just minutes before the crash.

Three audio recordings between Madrid's control centre and two train drivers appear to show that one high-speed train was given clearance to move even though another train had stalled on the track, about 25km (15 miles) ahead.
Puente had said that the decision to instruct the trains to move again, without any speed restrictions, was "inexplicable".

The leaking of the audio recordings has been criticised by some Spanish politicians, with Alberto Ibáñez, a member of Congress for the left-wing Sumar platform, writing on X that they were "despicable".

Meanwhile, Irene Montero - the prime ministerial candidate for the left-wing Podemos party - said responsibility for the crash should not be placed on one worker, adding that train drivers and experts have been warning against the liberalisation of the railway sector for years.
On Friday Puente said he was "not going to use any worker as a shield".
But he said "many questions" arose as a result of the tragedy and he wanted to look at them "one by one".
"If the investigation shows there is human error we will act in consequence of that," he said.
The country is observing three days of mourning, as the families of victims and the survivors of the crash struggle to comprehend how it could have happened.
The conservative People's Party joined calls for Puente's resignation after trade union CSIF called for the same earlier this week.
But Puente said on Friday he would not budge from his position.
"The easy thing for me would be to leave, but neither that fits with my character nor is it what the Prime Minister has asked me to do," he said.
"I feel immense pain and immense sadness for the victims and their relatives... I cannot let this pain paralyse me though. We have to find solutions to this problem."
Additional reporting by Sergi Forcada Freixas

articles.title: Canadian economy stalled in August, points to September decline: StatsCan
articles.summary: Statistics Canada GDP data for August shows economic growth was essentially flat in August despite a rebound in retail trade that more than offset a decline in July. Wholesale trade, meanwhile, fell…

image.caption: Linamar employees assemble components of a light truck transmission on the floor of a Linamar factory, in Guelph, Ont., on Feb. 6, 2025. Statistics Canada GDP data showed that a reduction in wholesale trade, including in motor vehicle parts, declined in August. (Evan Mitsui/CBC)

blocks.text: Business·New

Statistics Canada GDP data for August shows economic growth was essentially flat in August despite a rebound in retail trade that more than offset a decline in July. Wholesale trade, meanwhile, fell 1.4 per cent in August, as most subsectors contracted.
Rebound in retail trade wasn't enough to make up for weakness in wholesale trade, public sector activity
Statistics Canada says the economy stalled for a second month in a row in August amid weakness in the public sector and wholesale trade.
The agency says real gross domestic product was essentially unchanged that month despite a rebound in retail trade that more than offset a decline in July.
Manufacturing output has also grown in five of the last seven months, while a solid month on the railways drove gains in transportation and warehousing.
Wholesale trade, meanwhile, fell 1.4 per cent in August, as most subsectors contracted.
Work to prepare the 2026 census was also winding down in the month, driving widespread contractions in public administration.
StatsCan's early estimates for September suggest real GDP declined 0.1 per cent amid losses in manufacturing and mining, quarrying and oil and gas extraction.
Economists polled by Reuters ahead of the release predicted 0.2 per cent growth for August.

articles.title: Schools, officials prepare families for morning darkness after B.C. ditches fall time change

image.caption: Schools and officials are preparing families for dark mornings this fall. (Maryse Zeidler/CBC)

blocks.text: British Columbia

Sunday, Nov. 1, is around the time when most residents of B.C. would have experienced the fall time change. This will be the first winter in more than 100 years British Columbians will not be turning their clocks back an hour because the province moved to permanent daylight time.
Sunrise will be as late as 9:08 a.m. in parts of the South Coast this winter

The lack of time change this fall is prompting some schools, police and government agencies across B.C. to prepare families for increasingly dark mornings, hoping to keep children safe as they make their way to school before the sun comes up.
This weekend, residents of some provinces like Ontario and Quebec are turning back their clocks. But earlier this year B.C. moved to permanent daylight time.
The change means people in some parts the South Coast, like Vancouver, won't see the sun rise until as late as 9:08 this winter.
"That's definitely a concern," said mother Kim Robinson, picking her child up from Aspen Elementary in Comox.
"When I look at our wardrobe and stuff I think of colours, and how are we going to be more visible."

items: Why some scientists don't support B.C.'s switch to permanent daylight time

blocks.text: Some parts of the province, like Fort St. John, are used to dealing with dark mornings because they haven't observed Daylight Saving Time for decades now. But early commutes with no sunlight at all will be a first for many other British Columbians, after the province passed the Daylight Saving Act in 1919.
ICBC says its data shows that children are most at risk during their commutes to and from school. (Maryse Zeidler/CBC)
Building awareness about visibility
In Sooke, Victoria and Saanich, schools are partnering with the Capital Regional District on a new campaign. Lets Get Visible encourages families to wear bright clothing and reflective gear.
Some schools on Vancouver Island say they have been or will be giving students reflective gear.
The Victoria School District says it has been handing out reflectors to students to help keep them more visible during their commute to school. (Submitted by the Victoria School District)
Paul Block, superintendent and CEO with the Sooke School District, says the switch to permanent daylight time is a good time to remind the community about early morning safety around schools.

"What we're trying to get is a sense of awareness for our families that do walk, ride or wheel to school to really be thinking a little bit more about being visible on their routes to school," Block said.
"We also want to extend that to the greater community because drivers as well need to be aware of that to avoid those accidents."

items: For thousands of workers, lifelong time-zone math will go out the window when B.C. stops changing clocks

blocks.text: Crashes more likely during school commutes: ICBC
According to ICBC, for many children, getting to and from school is the riskiest part of their day.
ICBC says its data shows minors are more than twice as likely to be involved in a crash during their school commute than other times of the day.

items: Officials adjust border crossing hours as B.C. drops seasonal time change

blocks.text: Sooke School District superintendent Paul Block says educating drivers about the change in morning daylight is important as well. (Maryse Zeidler/CBC)
In Victoria, police are amplifying the early morning safety message as well.
"On [Nov. 1], our clocks don't change. Our routines stay the same but road conditions transition," said media relations officer Sgt. Kristin Greffard in a recent Facebook post.
"As the days get shorter, visibility becomes more challenging."

articles.title: Italy: Students and workers rally over living costs
articles.summary: Students and workers have marched across Italy for more school funding and relief from rising living costs. The rallies follow weeks of school occupations and protests against higher military…

image.caption: Students demanding education and housing support joined workers protesting rising living costs and military spending across ItalyImage: Andreas Solaro/AFP

blocks.text: Tens of thousands of students and workers marched across Italy on Friday, demanding more education funding and relief from rising living costs.
The rallies followed weeks of student tent camps and school occupations, with a general strike bringing workers into the streets alongside them.
Demonstrations took place in dozens of cities, including Rome, Milan, Turin, Bologna, Genoa and Naples. Police were deployed in large numbers after earlier protests descended into rioting.
Why were students and workers protesting?
Demonstrators criticized Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's right-wing government over low wages, rising fuel prices and military spending. Students demanded more money for schools and universities.
In Rome, university student Beatrice Chilelli said students were "at a breaking point."
"They can't afford to pay exorbitant tuition fees, and rent... which weighs heavily on their parents' shoulders," the 21-year-old told AFP.

blocks.caption: Like their French counterparts, students in Italy have been protesting for weeksImage: Marco Bertorello/AFP

blocks.text: The USB trade union called a general strike, with truck drivers, taxi drivers and farmers among those joining the protests. Disruption to public transport remained limited on Friday morning.
Thousands marched from Rome's Termini station past the Colosseum, accompanied by two tractors and a taxi. "We need more houses, not bombs!" one group chanted.
Did the protests turn violent?
Minor scuffles broke out between demonstrators and riot police in Turin at the start of the march. No major clashes had been reported by midday.
In Milan, the procession headed away from the city center, where rioters looted shops, damaged property and clashed with police after a cost-of-living demonstration two weeks earlier.
Authorities also increased protection around landmarks, including Rome's Colosseum and Milan's cathedral.
The student protests have drawn momentum from similar movements in France and Spain. Teachers, retirees and other workers also joined Friday's rallies.
France protests continue despite police crackdown

articles.title: Swedish academic says he has been barred from UK over event with Palestine Action founder
articles.summary: Andreas Malm was due to appear on a panel alongside a co-founder of the proscribed group next week.

blocks.text: A Swedish climate academic says he has been barred from entering the UK because he was due to speak on a panel with a co-founder of Palestine Action.

Andreas Malm told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that he had received a letter from the Home Office notifying him that his presence was "not conducive to the public good", with no further details given.
He said he could not "see any other explanation" for being denied entry than his scheduled appearance with Huda Ammori, a founder of the group, which is a proscribed terrorist organisation in the UK.
The Home Office said it did not comment on individual cases.

Malm is a senior lecturer in human ecology at Sweden's Lund University, whose work includes the 2021 book How to Blow up a Pipeline and 2025's The Destruction of Palestine is the Destruction of the Earth.

He said he had asked the Home Office to explain its decision, but could not see a reason beyond the upcoming talk in London with Ammori organised by the left-wing magazine Tribune - calling the move a "severe restriction on the free exchange of ideas".
Malm said he was not a member of Palestine Action, had never publicly endorsed it, nor had he given it any financial support.
"The only link to Palestine Action is her as a person," he said, criticising the UK government for ascribing "guilt by association".

The academic acknowledged that he had previously described the Hamas-led 7 October 2023 attacks on Israel - in which about 1,200 people were killed and another 251 taken hostage - as "fundamentally an act of liberation".

Malm said it was possible that these remarks, during a December 2023 talk in which he also condemned the "deplorable" killing of civilians in the cross-border attack, had been the reason for the Home Office's decision.
But he argued that these views had been in the public realm for a long time, including when he was last allowed into the UK to deliver a talk in May.

"I don't expect the British state to agree with me on Palestine or climate or anything. What I expect the British state to do is to continue to let me enter the country and to discuss with colleagues, with people who disagree with me - as I have done for years."

articles.title: Aid operation, evacuations underway in Ukraine's stricken city of Oleshky
articles.summary: Starving residents of a Russian-held town in southern Ukraine began evacuating on Friday as part of a joint relief operation by the opposing sides, the first of its kind in more than four years of…

image.caption: Ukraine's Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets, centre left, and Russian Ombudsman Yana Lantratova speak with journalists before departing for Oleshky to evacuate local residents to a safe area during a local ceasefire in Ukraine's Kherson region on Friday. (Office of the Ombudsman of Ukraine/The Associated Pr

blocks.text: World

Starving residents of a Russian-held town in southern Ukraine began evacuating on Friday as part of a joint relief operation by the opposing sides, the first of its kind in more than four years of war.
Localized ceasefire holds for more than 3 days but attacks continue elsewhere in Ukraine
Starving residents of a Russian-held town in southern Ukraine began evacuating on Friday as part of a joint relief operation by the two sides, the first of its kind in more than four years of war.
Under a local ceasefire brokered by U.S. First Lady Melania Trump, an aid convoy arrived in the town of Oleshky and people were given the opportunity to leave if they wished.
It was the most striking example yet of co-operation between the two warring sides.
But attacks continued elsewhere, with Russian strikes overnight targeting seven regions as well as the capital, Kyiv, and the southeastern city of Dnipro, officials said.

Russia said it had shot down 1,043 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions overnight. On Thursday, a Russian drone strike killed at least 15 people on a crowded rail platform in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro.

In Oleshky, Russian human rights commissioner Yana Lantratova said groups of people were boarding evacuation buses — some wishing to go to Russia and others to Ukraine. A senior Ukrainian lawmaker also said evacuations had begun.
People stand next to a building in Kyiv, Ukraine, on Friday that was damaged by a late-evening Russian missile strike. (Valentyn Ogirenko/Reuters)
It was not clear how many people were in each group, and how many residents, if any, had decided to stay.

Addressing Ukraine's parliament on Friday, Prime Minister Sergiy Koretskyi said residents headed for Ukraine would travel through Russia to Belarus before entering the Kyiv and Chernihiv regions, news agency Interfax Ukraine reported.
Lantratova, appearing side by side with her Ukrainian counterpart Dmytro Lubinets, said food, hygiene products, medical supplies and fuel were being delivered to the town.
Lubinets said everyone in need of assistance would get it.

"We have reached an agreement to assist citizens who wish to travel to Ukraine — they will be provided with the opportunity to do so. Likewise, assistance will be available to those who wish to travel to the Russian Federation," he said.

items: Russian drone strike kills at least 14 on Ukrainian rail platform
Russia, Ukraine begin ceasefire in city of Oleshky as deadly strikes continue elsewhere

blocks.text: In footage posted by Lubinets, teary-eyed residents warmly greeted the Ukrainian delegation.
Oleshky, on the Dnipro River opposite the city of Kherson, was seized by Russian troops during the first days of their full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
It has suffered extensive damage and was badly flooded after the destruction of the huge upriver Kakhovka dam in 2023.

Residents have given harrowing accounts of risking their lives travelling along mine-strewn roads — one known as the "road of death" — just to get food and water. Some say they have survived on a cup of rice or buckwheat a day, sometimes with a tomato, cucumber or wild plants added.
A local ceasefire came into force in Oleshky and the Kherson region early on Tuesday.
"This is the first time since 2022 that a ceasefire has been established across such an extensive stretch of the front line and has been maintained for such a significant duration," Lubinets said.
The arrival of the aid convoy was preceded by demining operations in which Lantratova said a sapper and one other person were killed.
Melania Trump-brokered ceasefire area expands in eastern Ukraine

She said 25 buses were on hand to evacuate people, with special provision for those who were bedridden, and 50 medical personnel were present. There was even a bus with pet cages for those who wished to take their animals with them.

The joint relief operation offers hope that the two sides are capable of working together, despite the ferocity of the war, in which both sides have intensified long-range airstrikes while battlefield front lines remain largely static.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said there was a "high degree of co-ordination" between Lantratova and Lubinets.
U.S.-mediated peace talks are due to resume next month in Abu Dhabi for the first time since February, as U.S. President Donald Trump seeks to end a conflict he once said he could solve in a day.

Russia still hopes that Trump can pressure Kyiv into accepting a deal that meets many of Moscow's conditions, such as full Russian control of Ukraine's Donbas region and a ban on Ukraine joining NATO.

Kyiv wants to ensure that U.S. intelligence-sharing continues, along with full access to Elon Musk's recently disrupted battlefield communications system, Starshield, and that European-bought U.S. military hardware, including Patriot interceptor missiles, continues to flow.

articles.title: China denies allegations of spy operation targeting Nvidia CEO
articles.summary: US intelligence officials believe a Chinese businesswoman was gathering information for Beijing on the US chip-making giant, The New York Times reports.

blocks.text: China has rejected allegations of a Chinese espionage operation targeting Nvidia's chief executive, Jensen Huang, describing the claims as "groundless speculation".

US intelligence officials believe that Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman linked to Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed, was gathering information for Beijing on the US chip-making giant, according to a report by The New York Times, external.

The report said Alice Huang, who is of no relation to Jensen Huang, was under investigation over the possible diversion of advanced Nvidia AI chips to China and had developed a close relationship with Jensen.
Nvidia said their interactions were routine business engagements, while Beijing accused Washington of attempting to smear China. Alice Huang did not respond to the paper's request for comment.
The BBC has contacted Megaspeed and the White House for comment.
US intelligence agencies had been monitoring Alice Huang and concluded that she was acting on behalf of the Chinese government, according to unnamed sources cited by The New York Times.
Surveillance reportedly revealed communications between Alice Huang and an American citizen, who was subsequently identified as Jensen Huang through a process known as "unmasking".
It remains unclear what information Alice Huang - who is also known as Huang Le - allegedly passed to Beijing, how valuable it was, or when she is believed to have begun gathering intelligence.
At a regular briefing on Friday, Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said: "The report in question is based on groundless speculation and is nothing more than an attempt to smear China."
The paper's report comes amid longstanding US concerns about China's access to advanced computing technology, which is considered crucial to developing artificial intelligence systems.
Jensen Huang has argued that allowing Nvidia to sell more of its products to China is important for maintaining US competitiveness in the global AI industry.

But Washington has restricted exports of the most advanced Nvidia chips to China since 2022, citing national security concerns and the risk that the technology could strengthen China's military operations. There have however been some loosening of restrictions during Trump's administration.

US officials said they had caught several firms illegally trafficking the chips across the Chinese border. They have also investigated whether companies operating through third countries are helping Chinese businesses access the restricted technology.
Nvidia has said it complies with applicable export laws and that there is no evidence its chips have been smuggled into China.
In response to the allegations made by the Times, John Rizzo, a spokesman for Nvidia, said: "Jensen's interactions with Ms Huang are not unusual or unexpected".
He said customers like Megaspeed "receive ordinary business information - not sensitive Nvidia trade secrets - and zero information relevant to national security."
He added that allegations the Singaporean company was smuggling chips to China "were thoroughly investigated and debunked last year".

Megaspeed told the paper its current leadership took the allegations seriously and had appointed external legal advisers to conduct an internal investigation. The company also said it had informed the US government that it was willing to cooperate.
It is unclear how closely Alice Huang remains involved with Megaspeed.

articles.title: Gulf states must rethink trillion-dollar defence in light of US-Iran war, says report
articles.summary:
IISS study questions over-reliance on American support and ‘over-dependence on expensive, high-end systems’

Gulf states are going to have to reconfigure their trillion-dollar defences given…

blocks.text: Gulf states are going to have to reconfigure their trillion-dollar defences given the damage inflicted on their economies and the questionable continued value of US bases in the face of Iranian attack, according to a study by the International Institute for Strategic Studies.

The report says that in the weeks before the 8 April ceasefire, 12 regional states, overwhelmingly in the Gulf, faced 4,670 Iranian one-way attack drones and more than 1,400 ballistic missiles. Nearly half were aimed at the United Arab Emirates. Although the vast majority were repelled, one estimate of the damage to energy infrastructure cited by the report is put as high as $58bn (£43bn).

Iran would portray either a reduction or complete withdrawal of US forces from the Gulf region as “a strategic success and vindication of its steadfastness, but also use it to embarrass the Gulf states about their decades-long courtship of US protection”.

The report says the war also highlights another “uncomfortable truth for the Gulf states: not only has their trillion-dollar acquisition of US weapons not translated into US protection at the crucial time, but their respective militaries are also not adequately prepared for the new kind of attritional air war to which they are being exposed”.

Despite huge investment in mainly US armaments, the report identified significant shortcomings: “overwhelming reliance on US-supplied air- and missile-defence systems and munitions; a failure to achieve regional defence integration; a shortage of minesweeping capability; limited retaliatory options; and the prohibitive costs stemming from an over-dependence on expensive, high-end systems to take down relatively inexpensive drones and missiles”.

The report is neutral on whether the divided Gulf states should seek a new non-aggression pact with Iran, but notes that the US-Iran war has shown that longstanding defence and security partnerships with the US “have failed to ensure adequate protection against Iranian aggression …
“If anything, US military bases and defence partnerships with the US have provided Iran with another pretext for attacks against the Gulf states.”
Public opinion on the US in the Gulf has also been shifting, “from security provider to strategic liability”.

Any reduction or withdrawal of US forces from the Gulf region would be portrayed by Iran “as a strategic success and vindication of its steadfastness” and would also be used “to embarrass the Gulf states about their decades long courtship of US protection,” the report notes.

The study comes after Chris Murphy, the Democrat senator and member of the senate foreign relations committee, said a live debate was under way in the US military about the value of seeking to rebuild the damaged US bases in the Gulf.

He said the Gulf state leadership “want us to rebuild” and “to keep a presence in the region”, but said: “What good is it to have a base in the region to protect American interests if within 24 hours of a hot war starting, it is wiped off the map?
“We would be criminally incompetent as stewards of taxpayer dollars if we were to rebuild bases that are blown up within hours of the next war starting.

“So clearly, we are going to have to have a smaller footprint in the region, and the limiting principle on the footprint that we rebuild will be ‘What can we protect?’ because we clearly cannot protect the scope of our footprint today and if we can’t protect it, it is useless.”
He suggested that, at the very least, the US may need to relocate its bases in the eastern Mediterranean further away from Iranian missiles.

articles.title: Hong Kong fire exposes entrenched triad networks in building renovation industry
articles.summary: The government proposes to make bid-rigging in building renovation a criminal offense, punishable by up to 10 years in prison and a HK$10 million fine. Laws against triads will also be tightened.

blocks.text: AFTERMATH. A drone view shows Wang Fuk Court apartment complex after a deadly fire last year, in Hong Kong, on April 16, 2026.
Tyrone Siu/Reuters
The government proposes to make bid-rigging in building renovation a criminal offense, punishable by up to 10 years in prison and a HK$10 million fine. Laws against triads will also be tightened.

items: A deadly fire at Wang Fuk Court in Hong Kong has revealed bid-rigging networks linked to triads exploiting the building renovation industry.
The Hong Kong government plans to criminalize bid-rigging in building renovations, proposing penalties of up to 10 years in prison and substantial fines, while also tightening laws against triads.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

HONG KONG – A deadly fire at a Hong Kong housing estate has exposed how bid-rigging networks linked to criminal gangs exploited weaknesses in the city’s lucrative building renovation industry to influence contracts worth hundreds of millions of dollars.

Organized crime groups known as triads were mentioned more than 40 times in the report on the government-subsidized Wang Fuk Court inferno, which killed 168 people and displaced thousands of residents.

In response to the report’s findings, the government proposed to make bid-rigging in building renovation a criminal offense, punishable by up to 10 years in prison and a HK$10 million ($1.3 million) fine. Laws against triads will also be tightened.

“After all these years, the syndicates are so sophisticated that they make use of all the legal loopholes,” said Chiu Yan Loy, founder and spokesperson of the All-Hong Kong Owners’ Anti-Corruption and Anti-Bid-Rigging Alliance.
Some networks delay distributing profits for months and use channels including cryptocurrencies, making money flows difficult to trace, he added.
Lawyers and law enforcement officers say the new offense will only work if it helps investigators gather hard evidence.

“We’re talking about offenses that exist in a kind of twilight world. There aren’t always transactions between offenders, bribery or a paper trail to prove collusive behavior or a cartel,” said one law enforcement officer, who declined to be identified due to the sensitivity of the issue.
Triad gangs — fraternal brotherhoods whose members swear blood oaths of loyalty and secrecy — have for decades been linked to extortion, prostitution, drug trafficking and loan-sharking.
Less prominent than in the 1980s and 1990s, they remain active and operate more complex white-collar scams, police and academics say.
The report explained that loose regulation and lax enforcement around vetting and hiring contractors let them enter the construction ecosystem.

Industry experts say bid rigging worsened when the government introduced hundreds of millions in subsidies in 2012 alongside a scheme requiring owners to repair buildings more than 30 years old, creating a lucrative market for contractors.
Tommy Leung, an associate professor at Wake Forest University, said his research showed renovation prices rose about 40% after the scheme began.
The Wang Fuk Court renovation, whose cost rose from an initial HK$152 million estimate to more than HK$330 million, provides a window into alleged methods used to manipulate projects.
According to the report, the alleged scheme began with gaining influence over the consultant who helps owners select contractors.

Will Power Architects secured that role with a HK$220,000 ($28,000) bid, well below an estimated HK$500,000 market rate, then issued misleading tender assessments, including giving main contractor Prestige Construction full marks for safety compliance despite previous convictions.

Authorities have brought at least 25 criminal charges related to Wang Fuk Court, which housed more than 5,000 people in eight 31-storey towers, against Prestige, Will Power and seven individuals. The report did not say whether the firms had triad links.
Prestige and Will Power could not be reached for comment.
Security Secretary Chris Tang, the former police chief, said on Friday, October 30, the government would “dismantle the criminal networks behind such activities.”

Hong Kong now plans to give law enforcement greater investigative powers, create a joint task force involving police, the Independent Commission Against Corruption and Competition Commission, and a new bureau overseeing renovation work.
Some former Wang Fuk Court residents were unconvinced.
“It’s just a slogan. They’ll say, ‘we’ll crack down on bid-rigging,’ but ultimately, nothing gets done,” said Betty, who declined to give her full name. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Tokyo thriller: Alex Eala exits Toray Pan Pacific Open after loss to Diana Shnaider
articles.summary: 'I didn't believe that I would be able to pull that win off because she played insane,' Russian Diana Shnaider says of Filipina tennis ace Alex Eala

blocks.text: RETURN. The Philippines' Alex Eala in action during the Stars of the Open exhibition event in the 2026 US Open.
US OPEN
'I didn't believe that I would be able to pull that win off because she played insane,' Russian Diana Shnaider says of Filipina tennis ace Alex Eala

MANILA, Philippines – Alex Eala suffered a heartbreaking loss against Russian player Diana Shnaider, 2-6, 7-6(5), 6-4, in the quarterfinals of the Toray Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo on Friday, October 30.

Eala had taken the first set convincingly, 6-2, but the second set saw the two players enter a thrilling tiebreaker, with Shnaider eventually forcing a deciding third set, 7-6(5), against the Filipina tennis star.
While the 21-year-old Eala had appeared to be catching up late in the third, Shnaider proved to be difficult to contain.

“Honestly, I feel like this match deserved to be a final. It was an insane level of tennis from both of us. I didn’t believe that I would be able to pull that win off because [Eala] played insane,” Shnaider said of her last-eight match against Eala, which lasted two hours and 52 minutes.
“But I was just trying to keep reminding myself to keep fighting for every point.”
Shnaider had previously beaten Eala in the second round of the Ningbo Open in China, 7-5, 6-4, on October 22.
The Russian player will now face Slovakia’s Mia Pohánková in the semifinals, while the Filipina tennis ace sets her sights on the Hong Kong Tennis Open. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Binance says $6.3B US hacked in what could be largest cryptocurrency theft ever
articles.summary: A U.S.-based blockchain intelligence firm says a North Korean unit was likely behind the hack that impacted more than $6 billion US on Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange.

image.caption: Binance in a statement early Friday that it was working with blockchain partners to freeze roughly $3 billion US in affected assets. The cryptocurrency exchange said that deposits were unaffected by the hack, and that will cover all losses. (Matt Slocum/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Business·New
A U.S.-based blockchain intelligence firm says a North Korean unit was likely behind the hack that impacted more than $6 billion US on Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange.
Binance says in new statement multiple 'points of breach' discovered
Binance in a statement early Friday called it a "complex attack" and said it worked with blockchain partners to freeze roughly $3 billion US in affected assets.
The cryptocurrency exchange said that deposits were unaffected, while withdrawals have been suspended and are expected to resume in the next day or two. It said it will cover all losses.
The company said on X Friday that an initial investigation suggested the incident may have involved a compromised laptop, but that a subsequent investigation uncovered additional "points of breach."

Blockchain analysis firm TRM, in a post on its website Thursday, attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, which it described as North Korea's elite hacking unit. "We make this judgment with high confidence," the firm said.
"An attacker moved approximately $6.36 billion US out of Binance wallets on 10 blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes," TRM said.
That would make the hack the largest cryptocurrency theft on record, it said.

items: Canadian 'tremendously sorry' after spending stolen crypto on Lamborghini, BMWs, jewelry

blocks.text: In February last year, another cryptocurrency exchange, Bybit, suffered a $1.5-billion hit when it was hacked. The FBI said North Korea and TraderTraitor were responsible for the hack.
"Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists, including the Bybit hack," TRM said.
North Korean history of hacks

Blockchain analysis company Chainalysis also believed the Binance hack was "likely done by DPRK group TraderTraitor," its co-founder and CEO Jonathan Levin wrote on X. DPRK stands for the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, North Korea's official name.

Asked about the potential ties to North Korea, a Binance spokesperson said only that the company is "working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of the criminals and bring them to justice."

Experts say North Korea has turned to crypto-hacking and other illicit cyberactivities as a source of badly needed foreign currency to support its troubled economy and fund its nuclear program in the wake of tough UN sanctions and other difficulties.

In December 2022, South Korea's spy agency said North Korean hackers had stolen an estimated 1.5 trillion won ($1.1 billion US) in cryptocurrency and other virtual assets in the past five years, more than half of it in 2022 alone. It said North Korea's capacity to steal digital assets was considered among the best in the world.

Changpeng Zhao, a Canadian businessman also known as CZ, founded Binance in 2017. In 2023, he pleaded guilty to a felony linked to failing to prevent money laundering on the platform and stepped down as the company's CEO. U.S. President Donald Trump pardoned Zhao in 2025.

items: Trump pardons Canadian Binance CEO who failed to stop illegal activity on crypto platform
What we know about ongoing Coldcard hack that's stolen over $100M worth of bitcoin

blocks.text: Zhao posted Thursday on X that "User funds are safe!" but added that the theft "does look like a hack on Binance." He added that while he doesn't manage Binance anymore, "as a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered."
The event, meanwhile, also raises questions about why stronger approval controls were not in place, said Kok Tin Gan, co-founder and CEO of cybersecurity firm NyxLab.

"This looks like one signature that gave the attacker a never-expiring, full-access token to a Binance hot wallet," he said, referring to cryptocurrency wallets that hold users' "private keys," or unique authorizations, digitally and which are connected to the internet.
Binance said on X it had "found no evidence of any wallet private key leak" and that the company would release more technical details when its probe is complete.

The MOU aims to increase awareness and compliance with the Social Security Act of 2018 among freelancers, ensuring they have access to benefits like sickness, maternity, disability, and retirement.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
The following is a press release from the Social Security System.

The Social Security System (SSS) and the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) on October 21 to expand social security protection for the country’s estimated 1.5 million freelancers and virtual assistants.
SSS President and Chief Executive Officer Victor Alfonso A. Limlingan and DICT Secretary Robert Joseph M. de Claro led the signing ceremony at the DICT office in Quezon City.

Limlingan said the MOU establishes a strategic partnership to strengthen the online freelancing industry through capability-building, competency development and expanded social security coverage for Filipino freelancers.

“A key objective of the MOU is to increase awareness, registration, membership and compliance with Republic Act No. 11199, or the Social Security Act of 2018, among freelancers and online workers, ensuring broader access to social security protection,” he said.
Limlingan emphasized the importance of extending social security protection to freelancers and virtual assistants, noting that they play an increasingly vital role in the country’s digital economy.

“Freelancers and virtual assistants are an important and growing segment of our workforce. By bringing them into the SSS coverage, we ensure that they, too, can access the same protection and benefits enjoyed by other workers—whether in times of sickness, maternity, disability, retirement, or even death,” Limlingan said.
He added that the partnership reflects the SSS’ commitment to leave no worker behind.

“Our goal is simple: no Filipino worker should be left without social security protection. Through this MOU with DICT, we are taking a significant step toward making social security more accessible, more relevant, and more responsive to the needs of our digital workforce,” Limlingan said.

Through the partnership, freelancers and virtual assistants will be encouraged to register as self-employed SSS members, making them eligible for benefits such as sickness, maternity, disability, retirement, funeral and death benefits.

As self-employed members, they may also apply for SSS loan programs, including salary loans, the Emergency Loan Program and the SSS Micro Loan Program. Members may likewise obtain additional coverage under the Employees’ Compensation (EC) Program for work-related sickness, disability or death.
The SSS contribution rate currently stands at 15%. For self-employed members, the Monthly Salary Credit used to determine contributions ranges from ₱5,000 to ₱35,000.
Limlingan said the lowest monthly contribution is ₱760, consisting of ₱750 for the regular SSS contribution and ₱10 for the Employees’ Compensation contribution.
“The highest monthly contribution is ₱5,280, composed of ₱3,000 for the regular SSS contribution, ₱30 for the EC contribution and ₱2,250 for the Mandatory Provident Fund,” he said.

Under the MOU, the SSS and DICT will also explore joint initiatives on freelancer education, partnerships, job creation and matching, advocacy activities and the monitoring of program outcomes to support the growth and sustainability of the freelancing ecosystem. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Germany takes cautious approach on Israeli election results
articles.summary: German politicians have been slow to respond as they wait to see who is likely to comprise the next coalition. Many are also hoping for a government without religious hardliners.

image.caption: No candidate in Israel has a clear path to powerImage: David Goldman/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Though it has been two days since Israel's parliamentary elections, German politicians are still being cautious to respond, as it is still unclear who will lead the new government. Although the right-wing bloc including religious hardliners led by incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is ahead of the opposition bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, neither has a clear path to a governing majority in the Knesset. Forming a coalition government is likely to be extremely difficult.

Martin Giese, spokesperson for German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul, declined to comment at Wednesday's regular government press conference in Berlin. but he did stress that Germany has been in contact with numerous officials and politicians in Israel via Germany's ambassador. "The Jewish state and Germany are inextricably linked by our history, and we will do everything we can to work well with any future government," Wadephul said.
No clear winner emerges in Israel's election
Alabali Radovan: 'Winter in Gaza will be difficult'
One concern for the German government is providing aid to the people in Gaza, and protracted coalition negotiations could delay necessary progress.

"Winter is coming, and it will be difficult," Development Minister Reem Alabali Radovan, currently visiting Lebanon, warned in an interview with Politico. She underlined that there must be more opportunities for aid organizations to provide crucial assistance in Gaza — and that it cannot wait for coalition negotiations.

In interviews with DW and broadcaster RTL, she spoke about the recent increase in attacks by Israeli settlers in the West Bank and east Jerusalem on Palestinian residents: "The radical settler violence must be stopped. The Netanyahu government remains in office on an interim basis, and this means that this situation must still be brought to an end." All settlement activity in the occupied Palestinian territories is considered illegal under international law.
More distanced from Netanyahu's government

Relations between Germany and Israel have long been particularly close — in part due to Germany's historical responsibility for the murder of millions of European Jews during the Nazi era. Recently, however, the German government has distanced itself from Netanyahu's policies, at least in its public rhetoric.

Most recently, Wadephul said after a major Israeli military operation near the city of Hebron: "Under international law, Israel is quite clearly obligated to uphold and protect the rights of Palestinians as well." Around 3,000 Palestinians were driven from their homes during the operation, which followed the reported killing of two Israeli soldiers by Palestinians.

In Berlin, there has long been speculation about whether Germany's policy toward Israel might change after the election. So far, one thing is clear: Unlike numerous other countries, including some in Europe, Germany does not intend to recognize a Palestinian state for the time being.
Israeli army demolishes Palestinian buildings in Hebron
CDU hoping for a centrist government
At the same time, Germany hopes that the future government will no longer include religious extremist, and in some cases far-right, politicians such as the current Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich.

"I think it would be best for Israel to form a government that is closer to the center of the political spectrum," Jürgen Hardt, foreign policy expert for the conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU) in the Bundestag, told DW. "Of course, that's something the people — and above all, the elected politicians — will have to figure out. But it's encouraging that so many people participated in the election."

The Arab-majority parties led by Palestinian citizens of Israel made big gains in this election. They are usually classified as part of the current opposition camp. Many analysts have noted that the historic results by these parties could lead them to play a kingmaker role in coalition formation.

However, Netanyahu’s bloc and various parties have ruled out working with the Arab-majority parties. Eisenkot's bloc has not stated whether it would be willing to form such a coalition, but one of the Arab-majority parties, United Arab List, featured a Jewish candidate, and has stated its willingness to work with Eisenkot’s bloc to unseat Netanyahu.

Hardt believes a minority government led by Eisenkot and supported by parties representing Arab Israelis is conceivable. "The major campaign carried out by Netanyahu's camp, aimed primarily against Arab Israelis, greatly mobilized the opposition, to the point where his camp no longer has a majority." The vice president of the German Bundestag, Green Party politician Omid Nouripour, told DW. "Frankly, after all the turmoil that has occurred — for example, regarding judicial reform — this is good news for Israeli democracy."
This article was originally published in German.
